entries.name: John Sinclair

expected_cases.sentence:
9½ to 10 years in state prison. Released on bond December 13, 1971 — three days after the "Free John Sinclair" rally at Ann Arbor's Crisler Arena (John Lennon, Yoko Ono, Stevie Wonder, Allen Ginsberg, Bob Seger, Phil Ochs and others, before 15,000 people) — after serving about 29 months.

Verdict as recorded: Convicted July 1969. The conviction was overturned by the Michigan Supreme Court on March 9, 1972 (People v. Sinclair), which struck down the state's marijuana statute as unconstitutional.

Charges as recorded: Possession of marijuana — for giving two joints to undercover Detroit narcotics officers in December 1966 (his third marijuana charge).

updates.charges: Possession of marijuana (reduced from sales charge)
updates.sentence: Six months in the Detroit House of Correction, followed by probation. Sinclair stated that he served the six months, entering in February 1966 and leaving in August 1966.

entries.rationale: Own1971essay paragraphs116–121 explicitly served sixmonths, lockedupFebruary andoutAugust1966.

entries.name: Frank George Holloway

expected_cases.charges: Freedom Ride participation — challenging segregated interstate-terminal facilities, Jackson, May 24, 1961.
expected_cases.convicted: Unresolved — the arrest is documented; the disposition is not established in the CRDL record
expected_cases.sentence: Arrested 1961-05-24. The Civil Rights Digital Library establishes the arrest and the identification photograph but not the disposition, any transfer to Parchman, or the release date — unresolved pending court, jail, or penitentiary records.

updates.charges: Refusing to obey an officer during Gadsden, Alabama lunch-counter sit-ins
updates.sentence: Jailed during the Gadsden lunch-counter sit-ins from November 28 to December 7, 1962. The contemporary Student Voice report distinguishes his release from the December 4 release of other demonstrators. Individual sentence and final disposition remain unverified.

entries.rationale: Student Voice Dec19,1962 pp1,3: Holloway arrested second wave Nov28; individual release Dec7, distinct from other prisoners Dec4. Original printed page3 visually verified in holloway1962-page3.png.

entries.name: Mary Lucille Hamilton

expected_cases.charges: Freedom Ride participation — arrested Jackson, June 25, 1961.
expected_cases.convicted: Unresolved — the arrest is documented; the disposition is not established in the CRDL record
expected_cases.sentence: Jailed after the June 25, 1961 Freedom Ride arrest, held in Jackson and Hinds County custody and transferred to Parchman. In her contemporary account, Freedom Riders Speak for Themselves, Hamilton explicitly dates her release to July 25, 1961.

updates.charges: Contempt of court for refusing to answer until addressed as Miss Hamilton
updates.sentence: Five days in jail and a $50 fine for contempt. The Alabama Supreme Court confirms that she served the five-day jail sentence. The exact release date remains unverified.
updates.convicted: Convicted of contempt; the Alabama Supreme Court upheld the finding in September 1963.

entries.rationale: Ex parte Hamilton156So2d926(Ala1963): five-day jail sentence plus$50fine; explicitly states she has served jail sentence. Habeas hearing June25th; contempt finding and remand to jail; release after five days on appeal.

entries.name: Fred Moore

expected_cases.charges: Arrest while inquiring at Albany police station about imprisoned peace walkers.
expected_cases.sentence: Held for two days and released on Christmas morning, December 25, 1963.

updates.charges: Refusal to perform assigned civilian alternative service under the Selective Service System
updates.sentence: Two years. Served at Allenwood Federal Prison Camp and released in April 1967 with good-time credit. Exact admission and release days remain unknown.

entries.rationale: Live read-only refresh confirms only Albany December23-25,1963 case, no draft case; all Moore-name profiles queried no second Fred. Identity link: Militant Albany report names Fred Moore Jr; AP places Voluntown resident with CNVA; contemporary Post interview names Fred Moore Jr of Arlington formerly CNVA Voluntown, Cuba-walk participant. Post Oct21,1965 three-hour trial immediate sentence, then began prison almost immediately (not enough exact admission); April1967 actual release explicit. Do not derive17months from24minus7 and do not modify Albany case.
